layout.hierarchy: Title is the largest and boldest element (dark red). The diagram dominates the middle by area. The red equation is the visual punchline (bright red, larger than the question text). The handwritten question is medium-sized black; the math labels (7, 3, X, =, +) are the smallest elements.

visual_elements.description: 3D volume multiplication diagram: (a) large orange/brown 3D slab (box in pseudo-3D perspective, darker top face) representing the RGB input volume; labeled 'RGB' above in handwritten font; '3 dims' written at its upper-left with a thin black arrow touching the slab; two small italic-serif '7' labels with tiny black arrows on its left edge and bottom edge (7x7 spatial extent); a cyan-outlined rectangular column drawn on its front face. (b) about 7 horizontal dashed light-cyan lines running from the slab's right side toward the filter, with a bold blue 'X' (multiplication) above them. (c) small cyan 3D slab (the filter/kernel) with darker blue top face, labeled '3' below (depth) and '7' at its right. (d) dark '=' sign, then a small gray '+' sign, then a neuron icon. Two thin black arrows: one from the bottom text area pointing up-right to the neuron icon, one pointing up-left to the '3' label under the filter.

visual_elements.description: Two thin black straight arrows with small heads: one starting above the question text pointing up-right to the neuron icon; one starting below/right of the filter pointing up-left to the '3' label

imagery: No photographs or clip-art; all graphics are flat vector-style shapes (3D slabs, dashed projection lines, circle neuron icon, thin arrows) in a hand-annotated lecture-slide style.

typography_notes: Title: bold sans-serif (Arial/Calibri-like), roughly twice the body size, dark red, centered, two lines, title-case with slightly irregular double spacing. Diagram annotations 'RGB', '3 dims' and the question 'How many weights for this neuron?' use a handwriting/marker-style font (Segoe Script / Comic-like), black. The '7' and '3' dimension labels are small italic serif (Times-italic math-variable style). The equation '7 · 7 · 3 = 147' is set in a rounded marker/handwritten style, bright red, larger than the question. No bullet lists appear on this slide.
animation_state: Slide appears fully revealed; nothing looks mid-build. The solid black bar across the very bottom of the frame is almost certainly the video player's progress/control bar rather than slide content.
recreation_brief: 1. Set the slide background to light gray (#E8E8E8). 2. Add a centered title text box at the top with two lines, verbatim: 'How many Parameters are  in the  RGB' and 'Image filter  ( K=3 )'; bold sans-serif ~32pt, dark red (#A61C1C). 3. Draw a white rectangle (~80% slide width, ~64% slide height) with a thin red (#C00000) border, centered below the title. 4. Inside the box on the left, build the orange input volume: a front-face rectangle plus a darker (#8A4D15) parallelogram top/side to fake 3D, filled #C07028. 5. Above it place 'RGB' in a handwriting font (e.g., Segoe Script), black; at its upper-left place '3 dims' with a thin black arrow to the slab. 6. Add two small italic-serif '7' labels with tiny arrows: one at the slab's left edge, one at its bottom edge. 7. Draw a cyan (#29ABE2) outlined rectangle on the slab's front face. 8. Draw ~7 horizontal dashed lines (#56C4F0) from the slab's right side toward the center, and place a bold blue 'X' above them. 9. To the right, draw a smaller cyan 3D slab (front #29ABE2, top #1B75BB); label '3' below it and '7' at its right in small italic serif. 10. Further right add a dark '=' text, then a small gray '+' text, then the neuron icon: a circle with a thick orange (#E8862E) ring and cyan (#29ABE2) fill. 11. Draw two thin black arrows: one from the bottom text area up to the neuron icon, one up to the '3' label. 12. Near the bottom of the box add the handwritten black line 'How many weights for this neuron?' (~24pt script font, centered). 13. Directly below it add the red (#D42A2A) equation '7 · 7 · 3 = 147' (~28pt rounded marker font, centered). 14. Optionally add a solid black strip across the very bottom edge only if mimicking the video frame; it is not part of the original slide.
